prompt: Which delivery type addresses an all-informed audience?
options: Offline archiving
Broadcast
Local storage
Unicast
explanation: Broadcast distributes traffic broadly, unlike unicast to an individual destination. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 12, 17.

prompt: Which services are identified among the E-LynX capabilities?
options: Only file storage with no network exchange
Voice, data and Blue Force Tracking
Only television reception for public broadcasts
Only analog voice without any data support
explanation: The lesson lists simultaneous voice, data and BFT among the system's capabilities. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 28.

prompt: What is the vehicular adapter's general role?
options: Removing all need for approved vehicle installation
Replacing all radio networking software with paper records
Mechanical support, power and control for the radio
Turning the handheld into a satellite without other equipment
explanation: The adapter provides support, power and control; its presence does not establish every system capability. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 47.

prompt: What is a purpose of the Test menu?
options: Determine a user's military rank from voice traffic
Check RX/TX paths and view diagnostic information
Automatically approve every maintenance action
Replace personnel authorization for protected settings
explanation: The source describes tests of receive/transmit paths and views of versions, counters and network performance. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 58.

prompt: Why distinguish voice integration from data integration?
options: Working voice proves all video and position data arrive
Success for one service does not establish the other
Voice and data always use identical application paths
Only data needs a receiving application
explanation: The lesson treats services separately; each required service needs appropriate integration and verification. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 72, 73.

prompt: A classroom MANET carries several sensor feeds. Reports compete for limited capacity. Which issue should the team examine first?
options: The age of the presentation describing the network
Traffic demand and required service priorities
Whether the sensors use the same display colors
Whether every report has an equally long filename
explanation: QoS addresses competing traffic requirements. Sensor integration also requires managing the volume of information; connecting more feeds does not create unlimited capacity. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 9, 12; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: A trainee says frequency hopping completes the security of an integrated information system. Which correction fits the lessons?
options: The communications waveform determines every user's release authority
Security review can focus entirely on the radio enclosure
Only the number of available frequencies needs further review
Other confidentiality, integrity and availability controls still matter
explanation: Frequency hopping contributes to transmission protection. It does not establish the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the complete integrated system. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 30; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 24.

prompt: A radio passes a repair check, but its sensor reports never reach the intended display. What remains unverified?
options: Whether the radio has a recognizable equipment label
Delivery of the required information to its users
Whether the repair technician completed a work record
The existence of a sensor in the classroom inventory
explanation: Repair verification and downstream sensor integration are distinct claims. The required information must actually reach the people and systems needing it. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 27; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 7, 9.

prompt: An integration exercise records strong RSSI and poor SNR near electrical equipment. What distinction helps interpret the result?
options: Received strength determines the sensor's observation accuracy
RSSI already expresses the information's factual reliability
SNR identifies the operator authorized to release a report
Received strength and signal-to-noise ratio are different measures
explanation: RSSI measures received strength, while SNR compares signal and noise. Environmental and electromagnetic conditions belong in the integration assessment; these readings alone do not identify a specific fault. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, page 56; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: Two systems exchange data through an integrator using TCP/IP. No voice call has been tested. Which claim is supported?
options: Every application requirement because one service succeeded
A completed voice requirement because transport is standardized
The demonstrated data exchange, with voice still unverified
A completed authorization review because data was received
explanation: The lessons distinguish communication services and application requirements. Standardized network transport and a successful data demonstration do not establish voice performance. References: MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 72, 73; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23.

prompt: What does COP stand for?
options: Common Operational Picture
Controlled Output Peripheral
Central Optical Processor
Combined Office Protocol
explanation: The Common Operational Picture supports shared situational awareness through integrated information. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 9.

prompt: Which listed device supports portable long-range optical observation?
options: Thermal Imager
Telephone exchange
Radio direction finder
Network switch
explanation: The lesson describes the thermal imager as a portable, battery-powered observation device. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 10.

prompt: What is an Interface Control Document used for?
options: Assigning classification levels without authority
Replacing all practical compatibility tests
Recording only personnel leave schedules
Defining interfaces and communication rules
explanation: An ICD describes how systems connect and exchange information so compatibility can be assessed. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: What is data overload?
options: More information than operators can effectively process
A guarantee that more data always improves understanding
Too few equipment labels on a storage shelf
The absence of any sensor observation
explanation: Sensor volume can exceed processing capacity; data management and analysis remain necessary. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18.

prompt: What does redundancy aim to prevent?
options: One failure compromising the entire system
Every possible failure under all conditions
All need for operator training
Any requirement to test replacement components
explanation: Redundancy reduces dependence on a single component; it is not an absolute guarantee. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: A sensor records observations locally during an exercise. The staff cannot receive them. Which capability needs attention?
options: The decision-maker's authority to change the mission
The wording of the sensor's equipment inventory entry
The number of copies of the training presentation
The information path between collection and intended users
explanation: Sensor integration includes downstream information delivery. Communications provides the links needed to exchange reports, coordination and feedback. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 7, 9; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 8.

prompt: A trainee turns one RDF bearing into a confident exact-location statement. Which correction is appropriate?
options: The report's arrival confirms that its location is exact
A bearing is an observation requiring further interpretation
One bearing supplies both location and a final intelligence judgment
Shared display access substitutes for additional source information
explanation: RDF provides direction rather than an exact position by itself. Observation and interpreted intelligence must remain distinct. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 10; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slides 10, 11, 13.

prompt: An integrator connects a new sensor network to an older service. Which document helps define the exchange at the boundary?
options: An Interface Control Document for the required exchange
A list of displays purchased for the training room
A maintenance record for the sensor's protective casing
A classroom attendance sheet for the integration team
explanation: The integrator connects different services; the ICD specifies the interfaces and communication rules needed to assess their compatibility. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 69, 70.

prompt: A computer can store every incoming sensor report, but analysts cannot keep up. Which concern remains?
options: The lack of a filename for each received report
The absence of any technical storage capability
The physical existence of the observation devices
The capacity to process and interpret the information
explanation: Computer storage is useful, but sensor volume can exceed the operators' processing capacity. Retaining records does not establish useful understanding. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 18; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 9.

prompt: During a classroom integration project, who should coordinate the communications and sensor responsibilities described in the lessons?
options: ASR and AIR personnel working through agreed processes
The inventory clerk replacing the technical and user teams
Only the computer supplier working from hardware drawings
Only the display operator deciding all integration requirements
explanation: The source assigns core C4 responsibilities to ASR and sensor/ISTAR responsibilities to AIR. Interoperability also requires coordination among people and processes. References: C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 27; C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18.

prompt: Which combination forms the C2 system described?
options: Only sensors and their transport cases
Only radios and their replacement batteries
Only weapon platforms and spare components
Networks, people, processes and command posts
explanation: C2 includes organizational and human elements as well as technical infrastructure. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7.

prompt: What does the combined system aim to support?
options: A collection of mutually unreadable information feeds
The elimination of all decisions by responsible people
Situational awareness and a Common Operational Picture
An equipment list disconnected from its users
explanation: The integrated capabilities support shared understanding and informed decisions. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 14.

prompt: What is standardized at Interoperability Points?
options: Only the model number printed on the equipment
Every internal technology in all connected organizations
Only the physical location of an office printer
The interfaces where different networks connect
explanation: The IOP concept permits internal differences while defining compatible connection points. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 17.

prompt: What does TCP/IP contribute in the lesson?
options: A replacement for every authorization decision
A standardized framework for network communication
A guarantee that all information is current and correct
Automatic agreement on the meaning of every data field
explanation: TCP/IP supports diverse systems communicating; application meaning and authorization require more than transport. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 23.

prompt: What does D3A stand for in the presentation?
options: Direct, Deploy, Duplicate, Authorize
Detect, Decode, Delete, Archive
Decide, Detect, Deliver, Assess
Discuss, Design, Document, Approve
explanation: D3A is identified as Decide, Detect, Deliver and Assess; this question checks terminology only. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 27.

prompt: An integration diagram shows radios, sensors and computers but omits staff roles and procedures. What is missing?
options: The automatic authority normally supplied by a network connection
Only another copy of the same network topology drawing
The people and processes needed to use the connected information
Only a larger computer for storing the same observations
explanation: C2 includes organizational and human elements. Connecting sensor information becomes useful through defined roles and processes, not equipment alone. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, pages 7, 9.

prompt: A trainee can view network diagnostics and assumes this grants command authority over all connected participants. Which distinction applies?
options: Equipment access grants authority whenever the connection succeeds
Viewing an interface record establishes responsibility for every user
Technical access and assigned command authority are separate
A network menu replaces the organization's assigned responsibilities
explanation: Diagnostic access concerns technical information. Command authority is an organizational responsibility and is not conferred by connectivity or menu access. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 7; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 54, 55.

prompt: An ICD settles message formats, but the two teams interpret the reporting procedure differently. What still requires coordination?
options: The human and procedural parts of interoperability
The availability of a computer to hold the document
The sensor's ability to produce a physical observation
The existence of an interface definition in the project
explanation: An ICD supports technical exchange. Interoperability also includes people and procedures, so a format agreement alone does not settle reporting practices. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 18; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 16.

prompt: A team wants to add a classroom sensor without replacing the entire information system. Which design principle supports this?
options: An assumption that any connector proves application compatibility
A policy of treating each upgrade as a complete system replacement
Open architecture with compatible, defined component interfaces
A requirement for identical internal designs in every component
explanation: Open architecture and modular design support additions and upgrades through defined compatible interfaces. They still require integration verification. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 22; C4ISTAR Sensors Integration, page 29.

prompt: A shared display worked at setup, but later information stopped updating. Which evidence best checks the feedback requirement now?
options: Observed delivery of updated information under the required service
The number of users who attended the initial demonstration
The original photograph showing the completed installation
The purchase record for the network's communication equipment
explanation: The feedback loop needs information about changing conditions. Current service observations provide relevant evidence; a past setup demonstration does not establish continuing updates. References: C4ISTAR Weapon System Integration, slide 25; MANET C4ISTAR Planning, pages 27, 67.
